name: Node Test Emulator
label: Node Test Emulator
description: Stateful BYO test harness for StudioQuack nodes. Runs PYTHON, JAVASCRIPT and TYPESCRIPT scripts against a mock studioquack helper, and has the SQS daemon build+run JAVA Build-tab apps (the daemon stages the context, builds on its own build network, runs the image as a hardened job sandbox with daemon-side mocks, and collects outputs — the emulator never touches an engine socket). Point a stateful instance at the `sq-local/sq-builtin-node-library` image. jobType is custom-script-executor because the platform has no dedicated jobType for custom-image stateful listeners — execution is the image entrypoint, not a Script tab. Do not use this node to call real sub-workflows; FUNCTION ports of the code under test are mocked via mock_function_responses.
author: 5c8b0d45-1d10-4f2e-844c-2318af96b2fa

ports.name: input
ports.description: Single object describing one test. Required fields: language, mode. Script-mode also requires script. Build-mode also requires files[]. Optional: input_data, configuration, mock_function_responses, expected_output, timeout_seconds. The daemon delivers this object as inputVariables.input (or currentNode.inputList targetPortValue=input).

schema.label: language
schema.description: Runtime of the code under test. EXACT accepted values (case-insensitive, stored lower-case): 'python' (CPython 3 via python3), 'javascript' (Node.js via node), 'typescript' (TypeScript via tsx, which requires() the CommonJS mock helper), 'java' (Build-tab / BYO Java app: the daemon builds files[] into an image, then runs+invokes it as a hardened sandbox). Any other string fails the emulator before the test starts (OUTPUT error port is set). Must also appear in the instance config allowed_languages (default python,javascript,typescript,java). Pairing: python|javascript|typescript MUST use mode='script'; java MUST use mode='build'. Example: 'python'.

schema.label: mode
schema.description: How to execute. EXACT accepted values: 'script' | 'build'. 'script' writes the source to a temp dir, generates studioquack_helper.py (python) or studioquack_helper.js (javascript/typescript), runs python3 script.py / node script.js / tsx script.ts with timeout, reads output.json (port→value from returnResult) and compares to expected_output. 'build' POSTs files[] to the daemon's helper endpoint test/build-run: the daemon stages the context, builds the Containerfile/Dockerfile with its own caps on its build network, runs the image as a hardened job sandbox with SQ_STATEFUL_RUNNER=true and daemon-side mocked studioquack.execute, POSTs a stateful invoke JSON to http://127.0.0.1:${SQ_APP_PORT}/invoke, collects outputs, then removes the container and image. The emulator deep-compares the returned output. If omitted, inferred: java→build, otherwise script. Mismatch with language is an emulator error. Example: 'script'.

schema.label: script
schema.description: Source of the node script under test. REQUIRED when mode='script'. Ignored when mode='build'. The emulator wraps it so `studioquack` is already in scope (Python: `from studioquack_helper import studioquack`; JS/TS: `const { studioquack } = require('./studioquack_helper.js')`). The script MUST call studioquack.returnResult([new studioquack.ResultItem(port, value), ...]) to publish outputs. Read inputs with studioquack.getInputValuesByPortValue('portName') (returns a list). Read config with studioquack.getParameterValueByShortCode('shortCode'). Call FUNCTION ports with studioquack.execute('portValue', payload) — returns mock_function_responses[portValue] or {} with a stderr warning when missing. Do NOT include CLI argparse / __main__ blocks; this is not a CLI runner. Variable and provider ports do not exist here and must not be referenced. Example Python: "vals = studioquack.getInputValuesByPortValue('in')\nresult = vals[0]['a'] + vals[0]['b']\nstudioquack.returnResult([studioquack.ResultItem('sum', result)])".

schema.label: files
schema.description:
Build-mode workspace. REQUIRED when mode='build' (language='java'). Array of {path, content}. path is a relative POSIX path without '..' or a leading slash (absolute and parent-escaping paths are rejected). One entry MUST be 'Containerfile' or 'Dockerfile' at the workspace root — the daemon builds the staged context with it. Include every file the image needs (Java sources, helper, pom.xml if used). The built image SHOULD follow the BYO contract: ENTRYPOINT is the app, ship curl, listen on SQ_APP_PORT/SQ_APP_PATH when stateful, or emit portValue:<port>:::result:<value> and exit 0 when stateless. FULL example: [{"path":"Containerfile","content":"FROM docker.io/library/eclipse-temurin:21-jre-jammy
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /app
COPY Index.class /app/
ENTRYPOINT ["java","-cp","/app","Index"]"},{"path":"src/main/java/Index.java","content":"public class Index { public static void main(String[] a) throws Exception { /* listen or one-shot */ } }"}].

children.label: path
children.description: Relative POSIX path inside the build workspace. Examples: 'Containerfile', 'Dockerfile', 'src/main/java/Index.java', 'src/main/java/StudioQuackHelper.java'. Rejected: '/etc/passwd', '../secret', 'foo\\bar'. Must not be empty.

children.label: content
children.description: Full UTF-8 text of the file at path. This is the file body, not a host filesystem path. For Containerfile include FROM/COPY/ENTRYPOINT so the daemon's image build produces a runnable image. Empty string writes an empty file.

schema.label: input_data
schema.description: Test values for the INPUT ports of the node under test, keyed by that node's INPUT port `value` (the port name the script would pass to getInputValuesByPortValue). Same semantics as the legacy Python emulator. Each value is wrapped as a one-element list by the mock helper (unless it is already a list). In build-mode these keys become inputVariables on the stateful POST and currentNode.inputList[].targetPortValue. Do not put emulator fields (language/mode/script) here — those are siblings. Example for a node with INPUT port 'in' whose schema has a and b: {"in": {"a": 3, "b": 5}}. Example with two scalar ports: {"name": "Ada", "count": 2}. Default: {}.

schema.label: configuration
schema.description: Per-test overrides of the node-under-test configuration parameters AND of this emulator's own config params, keyed by shortCode. Mock helper getParameterValueByShortCode(shortCode) returns configuration[shortCode] first, then input_data.configuration[shortCode] (legacy), then the fake template defaults. To override THIS emulator's instance defaults for one test, set the emulator shortCodes here: default_timeout_seconds, max_log_chars, verbose, allowed_languages. Example: {"operation": "Read", "timeoutMs": 2000, "default_timeout_seconds": 120}. Default: {}.

schema.label: mock_function_responses
schema.description: FUNCTION-port mocks. Key = the FUNCTION port `value` the code under test passes to studioquack.execute(portValue, payload) (or POST /v1/helper/execute {portValue}). Value = the object/array/scalar execute() must return. When a port is executed with no mock, the helper prints 'Emulator Warning: No mock response for function port \'<name>\'' on stderr, appends {port_value, payload, mocked:false} to invocation_log, and returns {}. Variable/provider ports are not mocked and not recognised. FULL example: {"log": {"ok": true, "written": 1}, "lookup": {"found": true, "value": "42"}, "search": [{"title": "n1", "url": "https://example.com"}]}. Default: {}.

schema.label: expected_output
schema.description: Deep-compared against the actual output (port → value). null or omitted = no assertion (output_matches=true if the process succeeded). Script-mode actual output is the object studioquack.returnResult wrote (every ResultItem keyed by portValue, e.g. {"sum": 8, "error": ""}). Build-mode actual output is the HTTP 200 JSON object keyed by the app's OUTPUT port names, or stdout markers portValue:<port>:::result:<value> when the image is a one-shot. Compare rules (legacy compare_outputs): type mismatch, missing key, unexpected key, array length, scalar equality. JSON 1 and 1.0 compare equal. Differences are strings like 'Value mismatch at root.sum: expected 8, got 7'. Example: {"sum": 8} or {"out": {"key": "orders:42", "found": true}}. Use null when you only care that the script exited and called returnResult.

schema.label: timeout_seconds
schema.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds for this one test (script subprocess, or the daemon-side image build + run + invoke POST in build-mode). Optional. When omitted or <= 0, the instance config default_timeout_seconds is used (default 60). On expiry the subprocess is killed (destroyForcibly) / the wait loop stops; test_passed=false and output.error names the timeout. Example: 120. Do not set this above the daemon's stateful request budget (default 300s) or the daemon will fail the node first.

ports.name: output
ports.description: Test report object (legacy Python emulator fields plus language, mode, build_log, image_built). Always present, including when the test failed. Downstream nodes should branch on test_passed (boolean) and read differences[] when output_matches is false.

schema.label: test_passed
schema.description: true only when the process under test succeeded (script_success=true) AND expected_output matched (or was null) AND the emulator did not set output.error. false for timeouts, non-zero exits, build failures, missing returnResult, or compare mismatches. Use this as the pass/fail gate.

schema.label: script_success
schema.description: true when the code under test ran to a successful completion: script-mode process exit 0 (or returnResult wrote output.json) / build-mode image built and produced an invoke body or stdout markers. Independent of expected_output. A script can succeed and still have test_passed=false when the compare fails.

schema.label: output
schema.description: Actual outputs of the code under test, keyed by OUTPUT port name. Script-mode: whatever returnResult captured, e.g. {"sum": 8, "error": ""}. Build-mode: the JSON object the app returned on POST /invoke (stateful) or parsed stdout markers (stateless). null when the process never produced output (crash before returnResult, build failed). This is the left-hand side of the expected_output compare.

schema.label: output_matches
schema.description: true when expected_output was null/omitted, or when deep-compare found zero differences. false when at least one differences[] entry exists. Does not by itself mean the script ran — combine with script_success.

schema.label: differences
schema.description: Human-readable compare failures. Empty array when output_matches is true. Each string is one path: 'Missing key at root.sum', 'Unexpected key at root.debug', 'Array length mismatch at root.items: expected 2, got 1', 'Type mismatch at root.found: expected boolean, got string', 'Value mismatch at root.sum: expected 8, got 7'. Walked like the legacy compare_outputs (dict keys both ways, then recurse; lists by index; scalars by equality).

schema.label: invocation_log
schema.description: Every mock-helper call during the test. Script-mode execute() entries: {port_value, payload, node_id, mocked}. Build-mode also includes {kind:'result', items:[...]}, {kind:'log', ...}, {kind:'fail', body}. Use this to assert a FUNCTION port was called, or to see which ports were called without a mock (mocked=false). Example: [{"port_value":"log","payload":{"sum":8},"mocked":true}].

schema.label: stdout
schema.description: Captured standard output of the script process, or the daemon-collected invoke response + container logs in build-mode. Truncated to max_log_chars (default 20000) with a '...[truncated, max_log_chars=N]' suffix. May include stdout markers (portValue:...). Empty string when nothing was printed.

schema.label: stderr
schema.description: Captured standard error. Includes 'Emulator Warning: No mock response for function port \'<name>\'' when execute() hits an unmocked FUNCTION port. Also compiler/runtime traces and container logs. Truncated to max_log_chars. Empty string when clean.

schema.label: error
schema.description: Failure message for this test inside the report (not the OUTPUT error port). Empty when the run completed without an emulator/process error (compare mismatches do not set this). Examples: 'script exited 1: NameError: name \'foo\' is not defined', 'timed out after 60s: python3 script.py', 'image build failed\n<log tail>', 'files[] must include a Containerfile or Dockerfile at the workspace root', 'Script did not produce output.json (returnResult was not called)'.

schema.label: execution_time_ms
schema.description: Wall time in milliseconds from the start of the test (after input parse) to cleanup. Includes the daemon-side image build+run in build-mode. Integer. Example: 842.

schema.label: language
schema.description: Echo of the language that actually ran: 'python' | 'javascript' | 'typescript' | 'java'. Empty only on emulator-level parse failure before dispatch.

schema.label: mode
schema.description: Echo of the mode that actually ran: 'script' | 'build'. Empty only on emulator-level parse failure before dispatch.

schema.label: build_log
schema.description: Present only when mode='build'. Full image-build stdout+stderr as collected by the daemon, truncated to max_log_chars. On a failed build this is the primary diagnostic (the report error also appends the log tail). Empty string if build was not attempted. Absent from the JSON object in script-mode so agents do not treat it as a script field.

schema.label: image_built
schema.description: Present only when mode='build'. true if the daemon's image build exited 0 and tagged the image (the container may still fail to start or invoke). false if the Dockerfile was missing or the build failed. Absent from the JSON object in script-mode.

ports.name: error
ports.description: Emulator-level error string. The port VALUE is the string itself (not wrapped in an object). Empty string '' when the emulator finished a test — including when the test failed; those failures live in output.test_passed / output.error. Non-empty only when the emulator could not start the test: request body not JSON, missing language/mode/script/files, language not in allowed_languages, mode/language pairing illegal, or an unexpected internal exception. Example non-empty: "input.language is required: python | javascript | typescript | java". Downstream error-boundary nodes should treat a non-empty string as 'do not trust output'.

schema.label: error
schema.description: Same string as the port value. Empty '' after a completed test (pass or fail). Non-empty concise message only for emulator-level failures listed on the port description. Never contains helper tokens or host paths beyond the temp workspace name.

configurationParameters.label: Default timeout (seconds)
configurationParameters.description: Wall-clock budget used when input.timeout_seconds is omitted or <= 0. Applies to python3/node/tsx and, in build-mode, the daemon-side image build + run + invoke POST. Accepted values: positive integers. 0 or negative fall back to 60. Default: 60. Example: 90. Keep this at or below the daemon stateful request timeout (sqs.sandbox.oci.requestTimeoutMs, default 300000 ms) or the daemon kills the emulator request first. Instance-editable so a slow Java build can raise it without changing every test payload.

configurationParameters.label: Max log characters
configurationParameters.description: Maximum characters retained in output.stdout, output.stderr and output.build_log. Longer blobs are truncated and suffixed with '\n…[truncated, max_log_chars=N]'. Accepted values: positive integers. <= 0 is treated as 20000. Default: 20000. Example: 50000. This is a payload/DoS bound — do not raise it unbounded. Does not affect the in-process kill of the script; it only caps what is returned on the output port.

configurationParameters.label: Verbose
configurationParameters.description: When true, the emulator prints a one-line dispatch trace to its own stderr (language, timeout, temp dir / image tag). That trace is captured in the stateful instance logs, not inside output.stderr of the test. Accepted values: 'true' | 'false' (boolean-like strings). Default: false. Example: false. Leave false in shared environments — temp dir paths are not secret but add noise.

configurationParameters.label: Allowed languages
configurationParameters.description: Comma-separated allow-list. input.language is rejected unless it appears here (case-insensitive). Accepted tokens (each optional): python, javascript, typescript, java. Spaces around commas are trimmed. Default: python,javascript,typescript,java. Example to disable Java builds: python,javascript,typescript. Example Java-only: java. Empty string falls back to the default four. Unknown tokens in this list are ignored at dispatch (they simply never match).
